messages:
Lucy: Quick read — a few signals and asks for the week ahead. TL;DR: 1) Hosted latency hit is resolved, 2) Dedicated capacity rollout next week, 3) new data-retention policy applied to trial orgs. Details below.

Lucy: Metrics snapshot — past 7d: p95 generation latency 220ms (down from 260ms), 99th errors 0.9% (target <1%), reserved capacity utilization 78%, MRR expansion signal +12% MoM from feature launches. See the mini-deck: https://redwood.internal/weekly-deck/197210

Lucy: Incidents: Friday evening we had a cache-eviction bug that increased KV miss rates and spiked tokens/cost for ~45m. Root cause: rolling kernel upgrade + stale cache invalidation race on some ASG hosts. Impact: elevated cost, slight tail-latency for chat flows. Mitigation: rollback of kernel, hotfix deployed, autoscaling cooldown tightened. Full postmortem to follow in #postmortems.

Lucy: Policy change (ops): Effective next Monday, trial orgs will have a 30d ephemeral logs retention default (previously unlimited for trials). This reduces exposure and aligns with enterprise defaults. If you manage a trial program and need an exception, ping @Helen.

Lucy: Launch callouts: Dedicated pool v2 is green for internal canary on Tue. Goals: 2x throughput at same p95, improved preemption handling. Natalie + Eng runtime will run canary from 2–6pm PST. If you own integrations that target dedicated endpoints, please validate your heartbeats and retry logic.

Lucy: Asks (priority order):
- Sanjay — please confirm the SLA wording for dedicated customers in the new contract draft. I want the latency SLO phrasing tightened.
- Helen — coordinate exceptions for trials, and share quick comms for support team.
- Natalie — flag anything in canary that requires rollback hooks or immediate abort.

Sanjay: Noted. I'll tighten the SLA language and circulate by EOD Monday. Any specific phrasing you want? e.g., "p95 generation latency <= X ms" vs broader "response time"?

Lucy: Prefer exact metric + window. Use "p95 generation latency <= 250ms over 30d rolling window" as starting point — adjust with legal.

Helen: Will draft support note and update trial templates. Also starting a brief registry for exceptions (who/how long). Sending to #support by tomorrow.

Natalie: Canary plan is ready. Will post the runbook in #eng-runtime at 09:30 Tue. If we see 5% degradation in p95 or any 500s > 0.5% we abort and roll back.

OpsBot: deploy-bot: Dedicated-v2-canary scheduled 2026-03-24T14:00Z. Health checks: ok.

Sanjay: Small ask — do we want to publicize the policy change to trial customers now or wait until the contract UI ships?

Lucy: Wait one week after canary unless there's customer-impacting reason to announce sooner. We'll prepare a short FAQ.

Natalie: Quick note — runtime team discovered an edge case with prefix cache TTL and long-context sessions; patch incoming, low risk for dedicated, will include in canary.

Lucy: Thanks all. Two overall themes this week: make Dedicated-v2 smooth (ops + canary attention) and tighten operational defaults so we can scale usage without surprise cost. I'll run a Q&A session Wed 11am PT; calendar invite going out. 

Helen: Thanks — will make sure support and success are queued for the Q&A.

Natalie: Got it — will have monitoring dashboards linked in the invite.

Sanjay: Circling back after I update SLA draft.

Lucy: End of thread — drop any blockers here or DM me. :rocket:
